rules.scientific_reason: Both readers decode the same stored NetCDF numeric payload; all three times and every required source field measured exact on the frozen official anchor.
Both readers decode the same stored NetCDF numeric payload; the complete three-time hybrid, lnsp, and surface source matrix measured exact on the frozen official anchor.
Temperature, horizontal wind, surface pressure, and surface height decode exactly across Rust GRIB and ecCodes for all three frozen CFSR times.

Specific humidity differs by at most three binary64 ULPs across all three frozen CFSR times; the worst points are tied to the same 5 hPa JPEG2000 message packing and have an absolute difference near 3.1e-25.
Pressure vertical velocity differs by at most two binary64 ULPs after equivalent decimal-scaled GRIB reconstruction across all three frozen CFSR times, so its existing threshold remains unchanged.

At exact source time, grid point, and native level the implementations share wind semantics; the bound covers FLEXPART binary32 storage and a small decoder rounding envelope without hiding interpolation errors.
Native-anchor temperature should differ only through FLEXPART binary32 storage and decoder rounding; the pre-registered bound is fixed before any FLEXPART numeric sample is observed.
Native-anchor specific humidity is a common source quantity; the absolute floor protects dry values while the relative term covers bounded binary32 storage and decode rounding.

Native-level pressure is common semantics but hybrid reconstruction performs several binary32 operations in FLEXPART; this fixed pre-observation budget covers that arithmetic without allowing level-order errors.

FLEXPART v11.1 constructs native hybrid meter heights with a default-REAL layerwise hypsometric recurrence anchored at its surface, while Trajecta uses the ECMWF alpha hydrostatic geopotential recurrence in binary64 and then converts height semantics explicitly. The observed bounded difference is therefore an algorithm-identity report, not evidence for widening the pre-registered common-height threshold.
Off-node common wind remains a hard gate, but the bound explicitly covers FLEXPART binary32 interpolation and the small local-basis difference from Trajecta spherical vector interpolation.
Temperature uses common scalar interpolation semantics; the fixed bound covers binary32 accumulation and minor bracket arithmetic differences but remains far below meteorologically material errors.
Interpolated humidity uses an absolute dry-air floor plus a relative term; the threshold is fixed before oracle observations and is tight enough to expose unit or level-selection mistakes.
Pressure interpolation and hybrid reconstruction involve several binary32 operations in FLEXPART; the bound detects wrong coordinates or units while allowing the expected precision loss.
The comparison remains in geopotential-height semantics and allows binary32 vertical interpolation, while a half-metre absolute gate still exposes wrong layers, terrain anchors, or units.

For hybrid above-sea-level samples FLEXPART first maps each source column onto its legacy fixed meter grid and then performs point interpolation, while Trajecta performs horizontal, vertical, and time interpolation against native hybrid ColumnGeometry. AGL and pressure-coordinate humidity remain hard-gated and pass; this ASL-only operator-order difference is retained at the unchanged threshold as a diagnostic report.

For hybrid above-sea-level samples FLEXPART first maps each source column onto its legacy fixed meter grid and then performs point interpolation, while Trajecta evaluates pressure against native hybrid ColumnGeometry before its own interpolation ordering. AGL and explicit pressure-coordinate samples remain hard-gated and pass; the unchanged pressure envelope is retained here only to quantify this ASL operator difference.

The registered pressure adapter calls FLEXPART verttransform_gfs and preserves exact native pressure-level wind identity; its mechanical pplev-to-prs bridge does not touch wind values, so the original binary32 native-anchor budget remains a hard gate without threshold changes.

The pressure adapter preserves source pressure-level temperature and only selects the frozen GFS vertical branch for downstream meter interpolation. The unchanged binary32 native-anchor envelope therefore remains an appropriate hard gate for ERA5 and CFSR pressure families.

The pressure adapter preserves source pressure-level humidity and does not introduce a humidity-specific formula. The original dry-air floor and relative binary32 budget therefore remain a hard gate for both registered pressure-coordinate source families.

The adapter's pressure bridge is a mechanical assignment from FLEXPART verttransform_gfs output pplev to the meter-mode prs consumer slot, with no pressure formula or unit change. Native pressure identity therefore retains the original hard-gate envelope.

Pressure-coordinate native anchors compare the same source geopotential-height field and do not use the hybrid hydrostatic reconstruction that is separately report-only. The unchanged source-height budget remains a hard gate for the registered adapter.

FLEXPART verttransform_gfs first remaps every pressure column onto one Cartesian z grid initialized from a single high-surface-pressure reference column and then runs its legacy point interpolation, whereas Trajecta interpolates against each point's native pressure ColumnGeometry. The unchanged wind threshold is retained only to quantify this compatibility difference; native anchors remain the pressure-adapter hard gate.

Pressure-coordinate temperature is remapped by FLEXPART onto a single legacy Cartesian z grid before interpolation, while Trajecta retains local source pressure geometry through horizontal, vertical, and time interpolation. This is an explicit compatibility measurement at the unchanged threshold, not a reason to alter Trajecta or widen the common-semantics budget.

Pressure-coordinate humidity follows FLEXPART's single-reference z-grid remap before legacy interpolation, unlike Trajecta's native local-column operator. The dry-air-aware threshold remains unchanged as a diagnostic scale, while exact native pressure-level humidity stays independently hard-gated.

The audited pplev-to-prs assignment is mechanically correct, but the pressure sampled afterward belongs to FLEXPART's legacy single-reference meter-grid remap rather than Trajecta's native pressure-column interpolation. The original pressure threshold is preserved only to report that algorithm difference; native pressure anchors remain hard-gated.

Although pressure-level native geopotential height is shared and hard-gated, FLEXPART's interpolated height is tied to its single-reference Cartesian z-grid remap while Trajecta evaluates local native pressure geometry and explicit geometric/geopotential conversions. The unchanged half-metre budget is retained as a compatibility report, not a scientific equivalence gate.

Trajecta uses the frozen full kinematic geometric-W chain and FLEXPART does not define the same quantity; analytic formulas remain the hard gate and this scale only organizes the external difference report.
Trajecta recomputes moist-air density from final pressure, temperature, and humidity, whereas FLEXPART storage and interpolation order differ; the analytic thermodynamic invariant is authoritative.

Trajecta deliberately converts geopotential to geometric height while FLEXPART orography follows legacy height semantics; common geopotential height is hard-gated separately and this value is report-only.
The near-surface algorithms are intentionally not FLEXPART-compatible in M3; analytic stability, continuity, and physical invariants remain the hard gates while oracle values are retained for review.
Surface-layer temperature uses a modern frozen similarity bridge rather than FLEXPART compatibility; the Kelvin-scale diagnostic cannot override the independent stability and continuity hard gates.
Surface-layer humidity follows Trajecta's frozen moist similarity bridge; a humidity-specific reporting scale is retained without treating legacy FLEXPART profile values as the scientific reference.
Surface-layer pressure is constrained by Trajecta's log-pressure bridge and final-state thermodynamics; the pressure-specific diagnostic scale does not replace those hard invariants.
Near-surface geometric W combines the frozen no-penetration and full kinematic contracts, which are not FLEXPART-compatible; only a velocity-specific difference scale is recorded.
Near-surface density is recomputed from the final Trajecta thermodynamic state, so a density-specific difference scale is reported while the equation-of-state invariant remains authoritative.
The geometric-terrain conversion deliberately differs from FLEXPART orography semantics; a height-specific difference scale is retained and common geopotential height is hard-gated elsewhere.
